title: ES Modules and CommonJS knowledge check

questions.prompt: What must be true for a TypeScript import to work in an application?
options: The source module specifier, compiler resolution, package exports and actual runtime/bundler must agree.
The compiler always rewrites every alias into a working runtime path.
Any filename extension works with every runtime.
Type-only imports create runtime values automatically.
questions.answer_key: The source module specifier, compiler resolution, package exports and actual runtime/bundler must agree.
questions.explanation: Type checking and runtime module loading are related but distinct responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “ES Modules and CommonJS”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with module-system differences and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with module-system differences and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Module-system differences”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “ES Modules and CommonJS”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check interoperability, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume runtime expectations is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check interoperability, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Interoperability”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
